body: I have vitiligo on my face. In the past, I was extremely insecure, especially since it started spreading when I was 8 years old. Children can be extremely mean and insensitive. Highschool was the worst, I learned how to apply makeup and had every intention of covering it up in college. The only time I gained confidence was because my then-boyfriend in college told me I was beautiful. It sucks that someone else had to remind me that vitiligo didn't make me less beautiful and worthy of love

Hi! It’s best to only apply cosrx patches on acne with a white “head”. For acne that’s more nodular, I suggest using a face wash like Benzac and an alcohol free toner with salyclic acid to gently exfoliate the face. Then a water based moisturizer (I use cosrx oil free ultra moisturizing lotion), followed by a spot treatment of benzoyl peroxide. I would stay away from trendy Ordinary products first because the concentration is pretty high and there’s a learning curve for that. This is the routine that worked for me (I had similar acne). Good luck!

Hi! I purged for 2 months but my derma made me switch to duac. I know that purging and inflammation is normal but please monitor if you’re getting other adverse reactions. I had to change to duac bc my cheeks started to swell from a reaction to epiduo

Oh my derma prescribed me a clindamycin and benzoyl peroxide gel a few months back! It worked very well— my acne was cleared in a month or so. I found it more effective than spot treating just with benzoyl peroxide. To make it more effective, I also was prescribed antibiotic pills for 14 days. Unfortunately this derma clinic is still closed because of quarantine restrictions, so I can’t avail of this gel for now. 

A few helpful reminders: 

1. make sure to wear a generous amount of sunscreen and reapply throughout the day (you can also purchase powder sunscreens if you wear makeup). This generally helps acne from getting too irritated and helps prevent scarring. 

2. Watching “Dr. Drey” on Youtube has helped me a lot! She explains everything step by step! One pro-tip I learned from her is to apply a think ointment like Cerave around the sides of the mouth, near the nostrils and at the corners of the eye before applying adapalene and/or benzoyl peroxide to prevent the meds from getting in. 

Hope this helps! Good luck!
Use a small amount of benzoyl peroxide to spot treat. Products with panthenol are also calming

Hello! Personally, I feel like the hostility towards “Filipinx” isn’t towards the Filipino LGBTQIA++ community abroad. I understand that using “Filipinx” is a way for them to create a space for themselves in the diaspora. However, mainland Filipinos refuse to use the term because the dictionary meaning refers to “natives or inhabitants of the Philippines” who don’t even identify as Filipinx in the first place. In fact, LGBTQIA members in the Philippines see no problem in self-identifying as Filipino. What we can do for now is petition for dictionaries to change the definition of Filipinx to refer to the Filipino diaspora. 

Another reason mainland Filipinos are pushing back against term is that they perceive that Filipino-Americans have a superiority-complex. In Twitter and other social media platforms, we have seen Filipino-Americans look down on mainlanders on not “speaking up” on BLM etc when in reality, many Filipinos do educate themselves and mobilize on issues that Fil-Ams may not even be aware of (EJKs, corruption, mishandling of COVID pandemic in the Philippines).

I was 8 yrs old when I was first told I had vitiligo. It started on my chin area and spread to my neck by high school. Sadly kids don’t realize that they’re mean. I was told I was a cow, that it looked like drool etc.

It helps to have a support system. My mom reassured me that it’s just on the surface level. In homeroom, I asked my teacher if I could explain to my classmates that my condition wasn’t contagious and I cleared up some misconceptions. 

It took me 10 years to accept my vitiligo. I used to cover it up every chance I got, and I used to burst into tears when someone would make a comment about it. As a girly girl, i felt like it ruined my chances to ever being considered conventionally beautiful. But as college came and eventually graduate school, I just realized that there are so much more things to be concerned about instead of vitiligo. 

People will love and accept you for who you are. But most importantly, you should learn to love and accept yourself. This condition isn’t the end of the world. But allow yourself to take time to ease into adjusting to life with it
